## 2026-09-20 — correction to two entries of 2026-09-19 (the keep-awake sentence)

Two dated entries above end their Method with "no keep-awake was started": the topology entry ("all agentic L7 traffic through
agentgateway-managed proxies") and the layer-attribution entry ("when one proxy carries the agent leg and the model leg"). Neither
entry is edited; this note is the correction, and the entries after them already carry the wording it gives.

What the record supports is narrower than that sentence. Those tasks' own scripts and commands started no keep-awake and changed no
power setting, and the Sleep, Wake, DarkWake and Maintenance counts they report are as they read them. But keep-awake is not claimed
absent: the agent harness that runs these tasks holds a rolling `caffeinate -i -t 300` under each active session process, an
idle-sleep-preventing assertion, as the entry on the chat span on a failed model call records with its `caffeinate-ps.txt`. In the
windows of the two entries named here the counts were not taken, so no figure is given for them; in every window counted since — the
pins of 2026-09-19 (19 of 71 assertion lines naming `caffeinate`), the worker's span on a second rebuild (21 of 25) and Experiment
A's re-run (115 of 284) — the counts and how they were counted are in that run's `host-sleep.txt`. Whether an assertion was held at
every moment of a window is not read from the log. No span, ledger or leg count in either entry depends on any of this.

## Experiment C / both receivers / observation — what did each layer record of one clean `SendMessage`, and what could it tell apart?

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2
- Environment: kind
- Method: the observation half of Experiment C as the author's note of 2026-09-20 puts it ("Experiment C on the agentgateway-only topology: what it asks now"), first cell-filling, on the standing cluster of the topology entry of 2026-09-19. The cluster was observed, not changed: nothing was applied, no manifest, fixture or agent was touched, and it was left as it was found — step 3, 5 HTTPRoutes carrying 0 retry stanzas between them, both receivers' injectors and the mock reset before and after. Certificates were checked first (`istioctl ztunnel-config certificates --node agent-mesh-lab-worker`: VALID CERT true for `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` and for the ingress's own identity). One clean `SendMessage` per receiver by the committed `experiments/gate2-single-clean.sh` with `RUN_ID=c1-2035` and `RUN_ITEM=2026-09-20-c1-observation`, one repetition each — `g2c-c1-2035-worker` (loadgen → `agw-central` → worker) and `g2c-c1-2035-orchestrator` (loadgen → `agentgateway-ingress` → orchestrator → `agw-central` → worker → `agw-central` → mock) — then `make export-trace` for each. Every layer was then read read-only, each reading written under the command that produced it: ztunnel's own access lines and `istio_tcp_connections_opened_total` by the committed `promq.sh`; the five `HTTPRoute` objects and both proxies' `/config_dump`; both proxies' access logs and every attribute on their SERVER spans; and the three ledgers by `make ledgers`. Versions were read from the cluster (server version, the istiod and agentgateway image tags, the Gateway API CRD's `bundle-version` and `channel` annotations) and the SDK pins from `go.mod` and `uv.lock`; no pin was changed. This task started no keep-awake and changed no power setting, and keep-awake is not claimed absent — in the window `host-sleep.txt` counts Sleep=0, Wake=0, DarkWake=0, Maintenance=0 and 3 assertion lines, 3 of them naming `caffeinate`, which is the agent harness's own.
- Result: both work items clean, 1/1/1/1/1 each (`summary.csv`) — that tuple is scoped to the named receiver's own ledgers, which is how `gate2-single-clean.sh` counts, while every "3 of 3 arrivals" below is path-wide, the orchestrator work item arriving twice: once at the orchestrator and once at the worker it forwards to. The filled map is `experiments/runs/2026-09-20-c1-observation/observation-map.md`, its counts `layer-counts.csv` (32 rows), and the readings behind them `ztunnel-access-log.txt`, `ztunnel-series.txt`, `routes.txt`, `config-dump-policies.txt`, `proxy-access-log.txt`, `proxy-span-attributes.txt` and the two work items' `ingress.jsonl` / `execution.jsonl` / `invocation.jsonl` / `spans.csv` / `trace.json`, under `experiments/runs/2026-09-20-c1-observation/`. **ztunnel (istiod):** on the 3 proxy→receiver legs the source named at the receiver's ztunnel is the delivering proxy — `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/agentgateway-waypoint/sa/agw-central` to worker and to orchestrator, `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/agentgateway-ingress/sa/agentgateway-ingress` to orchestrator — 3 of the 3 proxy→receiver legs `mutual_tls` and destination-reported, `destination_principal=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default` (the window query prints a fourth destination-reported row that is Prometheus scraping and not a leg, and a fifth `mutual_tls` series, loadgen → ingress, that is a leg and is reported from both ends); the two loadgen pods appear only on their own outbound legs and carry that same `ns/lab/sa/default`. Of the **165** ztunnel lines in the counted window — `kubectl -n istio-system logs ztunnel-tmzz9 --since=30m`, the same read the six counts were taken from, pinned afterwards as `2026-09-20T20:10:51Z..20:40:51Z` and re-counted at 21:04Z so the denominator can be re-run (`ztunnel-access-log.txt`) — 0 carry `http.method`, 0 `http.path`, 0 `SendMessage`, 0 `messageId`, 0 `taskId`; the work-item string occurs 18 times and every one of them is inside a workload or pod token, because this lab names the loadgen Job after the work item, so 0 of 18 are a property of a request. (A separate `--since=25m` read of the same log during the run returned 150 lines; that is the smaller window and not the denominator of these counts.) All 99 `istio_tcp_connections_opened_total` series carry the same 30 label names; the metrics-per-hop entry's 27 for the same family is a different reading of the same metric, not a change to it — that entry parsed the target's exposition, this one queried Prometheus, and a queried series carries the exposition's names plus exactly `__name__`, `instance` and `job`, with nothing missing the other way. **The routes (agentgateway's controller):** all 5 `HTTPRoute`s hold exactly one rule with exactly one match, `PathPrefix: /`, with 0 filters, 0 retry stanzas and 0 header, query-parameter or method matches anywhere — the same shape read back from both proxies' `/config_dump`. `route` is named on 8 of 8 proxy SERVER spans and 14 of 14 access-log request lines. One route rule keyed on nothing inside the endpoint: `lab/worker` alone carried 3 distinct path/method pairs in this window — `POST /` ×2, `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` ×2, `POST /control/reset` ×3. `A2A-Version: 1.0` was recorded on 3 of 3 arrivals, which is the receiver's own read of the header (`agents/worker/ingress.go` l.87, `agents/orchestrator/orchestrator/ledger.py` l.72); that the header was also present at the proxy, where a route match would run, follows from a reading rather than being one — 0 filters on 5 of 5 routes, so nothing on the path could have added it. **agentgateway's policy layer:** nothing was evaluated. Each proxy holds 2 policies, 4 in the cluster, all `AgentgatewayPolicy` `frontend` — `access-logs` and `tracing`, one pair per Gateway; in both dumps `"authorization"`, `"jwt"`, `"extAuth"`, `"rateLimit"` and `"a2a"` each occur 0 times, 0 route holds an inline policy, and the cluster holds 0 `AuthorizationPolicy` objects. **agentgateway's telemetry:** `src.identity` on 7 of 7 `agw-central` SERVER spans and 13 of 13 `agw-central` access-log request lines, every one `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default`; **0 of 1** on the `agentgateway-ingress` SERVER span and **0 of 1** on its access-log line, on a leg ztunnel reports `mutual_tls`. The two proxies' SERVER spans differ by exactly that one attribute — `agw-central` 17, `agentgateway-ingress` 16, the set being `duration endpoint gateway http.host http.method http.path http.status http.version listener network.protocol.version protocol route span.id src.addr src.identity trace.id url.scheme`. No A2A operation was recorded at either proxy: 0 attribute keys beginning `a2a.` on any span of either work item, `protocol=http` on 8 of 8 proxy SERVER spans, and `appProtocol` absent on 3 of 3 lab Services (the 57 `a2a.` strings in the orchestrator's trace are span *names* the Python SDK emits inside the application). **The application:** the ingress ledger's `remote` is the delivering proxy's pod address on 3 of 3 arrivals (`agw-central` on 2, `agentgateway-ingress` on 1) and 0 of 3 arrival lines carry any identity, principal or caller field — the 14 keys are `a2a_version body_len body_sha256 content_type id ledger logical_work_item_id messageId method phase remote source taskId ts_arrival`. On those same 3 arrivals the application recorded, before the SDK, `"method":"SendMessage"` 3 of 3, `a2a_version=1.0` 3 of 3, `messageId` 3 of 3 with `taskId` empty 3 of 3, and 3 distinct `body_sha256` values over bodies of 284, 296 and 315 bytes; the execution ledger then minted one `taskId` per dispatch, 3 of 3, and the invocation ledger carried work item, `messageId` and `taskId` together on 2 of 2 model calls.
- Interpretation: as documented, and the map's first column now says where the documented line falls on this topology. For this interaction only one layer on the path recorded which A2A operation had arrived, and it was the receiver itself: the operation lives in the JSON-RPC body, ztunnel does not read a body, the route's four match fields do not reach one, and agentgateway's A2A module was not switched on because no lab Service carries the `appProtocol` marking it keys on — so `SendMessage`, an agent-card `GET` and a control `POST` travelled one route rule as one undifferentiated stream of `POST /`. Identity is thinner still. Behind a proxy the receiver's ztunnel is given the proxy's SPIFFE identity and not the caller's, which is what Istio's L4 page states and what the topology entry already counted; and because every lab workload runs as `ns/lab/sa/default`, the one identity the proxies do hold separates no caller from another as this lab is built. The one reading this run adds that no entry held is the contrast between the two proxies: `agw-central`, whose namespace is not enrolled and which terminates HBONE itself, recorded a client identity on every request it served, while the ztunnel-captured `agentgateway-ingress` recorded none on a leg ztunnel itself reports `mutual_tls` — measured on 1 span and 1 log line, which is every request that took that path here. What a rule at either proxy would be given is a different question from what its telemetry writes down, and no rule exists to ask: the four policies the cluster holds are access logs and tracing, so nothing on this path evaluated anything. That is the whole of C's enforcement half and it stays unmeasured, together with the eleven other cells the map lists. What is true of all twelve is the brief's own stop condition — each needs a change to the cluster or a fixture — and not the narrower sentence the skeleton rightly keeps for the enforcement cells alone, that each needs a second operation on the wire and no fixture sends one: the A2A marking needs `appProtocol` set and then one `SendMessage`, the ingress proxy's `source.identity` needs one request plus a rule or a changed log template, and the status istiod writes on an `AuthorizationPolicy` aimed at `agw-central` needs no traffic at all.
- Follow-up: none. The preparation flagged four candidates and none of the four has a reproduction from this run, which is what rule 11 asks for before a draft exists: (a) agentgateway's `a2a.*` span and log attributes, in source and absent from the published attribute reference — unreproducible here, because the `appProtocol` marking that would emit them is absent on 3 of 3 lab Services; (b) the A2A page's examples sending the 0.x name `tasks/send` — a documentation gap that needs no cluster at all, its reproduction being the page itself, which the preparation fetched with its stamp and hash but this run did not; (c) the docs naming only the legacy `kgateway.dev/a2a` spelling where source also takes `agentgateway.dev/a2a` — the same, and untouched by C-1; (d) A2A having no typed CEL object or policy section where MCP has both — a feature gap whose report waits on C-8's result, which does not exist. `docs/upstream/` holds no draft for any of them, and this task filed nothing.

## Follow-ups 21 / both receivers / one rebuild — does the baseline script leave the mock disarmed, and does `make ledgers` now collect a resubscription's three ledgers together?

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2
- Environment: kind
- Method: three small changes to deployed paths, all three proven by ONE rebuild from a deleted cluster. (1) `experiments/gate1-baseline.sh` resets the mock before each repetition and, until this commit, not after the last, so the arming of the final work item outlived the script; it now resets once more after the last repetition of a run type that arms by work item, and after run 7. (2) the `Makefile`'s `GO_SOURCES_HASH` comment said a ko image's digest changes on every `ko apply` even from an unchanged tree; the follow-ups 19 reading contradicts that (11 builds at one (commit, `vcs.modified`) state carried one digest, and the digests that moved moved with `vcs.revision`), so the comment now says what was counted and why `GO_SOURCES_HASH` exists — the digest is not a content hash of the sources. Of that reading's two halves the comment now says which rests on what: one digest at one (commit, `vcs.modified`) state is 11 builds; the digests moving with `vcs.revision` is ONE pair in the same record, and it says so — one pair is what there is, not a series. The sentence was grepped for across the tracked tree on 2026-09-20 and again here: `Makefile` l.14 is its only live occurrence, and the run record that reported it keeps it as it wrote it. FOUR live locations state the same thing in other words from their own 2026-09-09 observation: the step-2c comment, the step-3 comment, `README.md`'s step-3 section and `experiments/scan-images.sh`. Three of them are dated, scoped observations of one repeat apply and are left exactly as each was taken, because whether the commit had moved between those two applies is not established in that record. The fourth, `experiments/scan-images.sh`, states the claim as a universal rule and prints it into every new scan record, so it takes a dated note of 2026-09-21 beside its own paragraph — the paragraph itself is not rewritten. (3) `make ledgers`' `sel()` selected on `logical_work_item_id` alone, so a resubscription's execution lines were never collected — `SubscribeToTask` carries no Message and so no metadata, and the execution ledger sits inside the SDK where no HTTP header is visible. `sel()` now selects a line when it carries the work item OR when it carries a `taskId` that a line of that work item minted **and names no work item of its own**; the map is built in one further jq pass over the same logs, an empty `taskId` is never a key, and the execution ledger was not touched. Both guards are about not merging two work items, and the anonymity one was added in the review round of 2026-09-21: without it a line naming a different work item is collected whenever it carries one of this work item's task ids, and symmetrically, so a later operation on the same Task given its own work-item id — a resubscription or a `GetTask`, which is a natural way to write a row — would silently merge the two collections. No committed script sends that shape today. The same round made a jq failure in the taskId pass detectable: the `||` took `sort -u`'s status, so a broken jq exited 0 with an empty map and the target fell back to work-item-only selection without saying so. The policy is the waypoint page's own recipe, "make the waypoint mandatory with an `AuthorizationPolicy` that allows only the waypoint's identity" (l.225), "enforced at Layer 4 by ztunnel" (l.245), with only the names changed: `selector: app: worker`, `action: ALLOW`, one rule, `principals: cluster.local/ns/agentgateway-waypoint/sa/agw-central`. It was applied at 04:21:04Z by `kubectl apply -k` from `overlay-c3/` in the run directory, and removed at 04:35:48Z after C-4 (next entry) by `kubectl delete -k`. The overlay is kept in the run directory and not under `deploy/`: CLAUDE.md proves a change to `deploy/` only by a rebuild from a deleted cluster and this task was not to rebuild; the committed overlays build to the applied objects — `kubectl kustomize` of each equals the `last-applied-configuration` recorded in `c3-policy.txt` and `c4-policy.txt`, although the C-4 patch file's comments were edited after the run (its line citation at 04:39Z, its count of outcomes in the review round) — so the later C step that wants this policy can promote them into `deploy/` in a commit that carries its rebuild — the recommendation. One work item per caller path to the worker: through `agw-central` by the committed `experiments/gate2-single-clean.sh` (`RUN_ID=c3`; it also sends the orchestrator's work item, whose worker leg rides `agw-central` too); direct to the worker pod and through the agentgateway ingress (`Host: worker.lab.internal`, its step-2c route, by `kubectl port-forward` as the lab's out-of-cluster sends are made) by `send-one.sh`, a driver kept in the run directory that sends what the load client sends — one agent-card `GET`, then one `SendMessage` `POST` — each as one `curl --retry 0` with `A2A-Version: 1.0`, `X-Logical-Work-Item-Id` and a `traceparent` whose trace id it records. Before the apply, one control work item each on the direct and ingress paths (04:20:44Z–04:20:46Z). The C-3 sends ran 04:21:17Z–04:22:03Z; the ingress path then took a second work item at 04:34:01Z, a different window 12 minutes later, because the first had ridden a connection opened before the policy (Result) — the wait was on ztunnel's own close line for that connection, not on a timer. Readings, each under its command and read stamp: `make ledgers` per work item; the policy object and status and ztunnel's own copy (`istioctl ztunnel-config policy`); istiod's log from the apply; ztunnel's log on the node that runs the worker and both proxies; both proxies' access lines and SERVER spans by the trace id each send carried (`proxy-spans.sh`); every arrival at the worker by time. Counts by `counts.sh` from the run directory alone. Versions read from the cluster and the lock files into `versions.txt`; no pin was changed. No retry logic, and every curl this task wrote is `--retry 0`. This task started no keep-awake and changed no power setting, and keep-awake is not claimed absent — in the run window `host-sleep.txt` counts Sleep=0, Wake=0, DarkWake=0, Maintenance=0, Wake Requests=0 and 18 assertion lines, 12 of them naming `caffeinate`, which is the agent harness's own.
- Result: run outputs under `experiments/runs/2026-09-21-c3-c4-ztunnel/` (`counts.csv`, `map-cells.md`, and the reading files each count below names). **The policy:** status `ZtunnelAccepted=True`, reason `Accepted`, message "attached to ztunnel"; ztunnel held it in the second of the apply as `Allow` with one rule, principal `Exact: cluster.local/ns/agentgateway-waypoint/sa/agw-central`; istiod logged one push naming it ("and 1 more configs"), and in it a 276 B workload (WDS) update and a 91 B policy (WADS) update to each of the two ztunnels (`c3-policy.txt`, `c3-istiod.txt`). **Controls, no policy:** direct 200/200 and 1 arrival, 1 received, 1 execute, 1 task, 1 invocation; ingress the same. **Through `agw-central`:** `g2c-c3-worker` 1/1/1/1/1 `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` and `g2c-c3-orchestrator` 1/1/1/1/1 `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` (`summary.csv`); all 3 of the worker's arrivals came in on `10.244.1.13:40711`, and the one `agw-central`→worker connection ztunnel logged in the window opened at 04:21:18.056Z (its close line at 04:24:01.963Z reads 163907 ms), 14 s after the apply; `agw-central` logged 6 `route=lab/worker` requests, 3 control resets 204, the card GET 200 and 2 `POST /` 200, each with `src.identity=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default`, and the worker's trace holds 3 `agw-central` SERVER spans reading 200 — 2 on `route=lab/worker`, the card GET and the POST, and 1 on the model route `agentgateway-waypoint/model-via-agw` (`c3-proxies.txt`, `g2c-c3-worker/trace.json`, 14 spans). **Direct to the pod:** GET and POST each curl exit 56, "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer", no HTTP status; `make ledgers` "no ledger lines of any kind"; ztunnel 2 inbound lines `error="connection closed due to policy rejection: allow policies exist, but none allowed"` naming `src.identity="spiffe://cluster.local/ns/lab/sa/default"`, 0 bytes each way, and 2 caller-side outbound lines `error="http status: 401 Unauthorized"`; no proxy on the path and 0 spans (`c3-ztunnel.txt`). **Through the ingress, fresh connection:** GET 503 and POST 503, body `upstream call failed: SendRequest: connection error: Connection reset by peer (os error 104)`; 0 ledger lines; 2 ingress access lines `route=lab/worker-ingress http.status=503 reason=UpstreamFailure` with that error and no `src.identity`; 2 ingress SERVER spans `http.status=503` with status error and no attribute naming the cause; ztunnel 2 inbound policy-rejection lines naming `spiffe://cluster.local/ns/agentgateway-ingress/sa/agentgateway-ingress` and 2 outbound 401 lines on the ingress's side. **Through the ingress, first send:** delivered, 200/200 and 1/1/1/1/1 — on the connection the control had opened: the worker recorded `remote 10.244.1.16:40457` on the control's two arrivals (04:20:45.997Z, 04:20:46.037Z) and on this send's two (04:22:03.292Z, 04:22:03.331Z), and the one ingress→worker connection ztunnel logged in the window (ztunnel numbers its own ports; the address above is the worker's record) closed at 04:24:03.545997Z after 197549 ms — opened at 04:20:45.996Z, the millisecond before the control's first arrival and 18 s before the apply — at level `info` with no error, 120 s after its last use. The policy was in force for new connections at that moment: the two direct connections were refused at 04:22:02.699Z and 04:22:02.779Z, half a second before this send arrived at 04:22:03.292Z. The connection this send rode was not closed when the policy arrived, and the request it carried 59 s after ztunnel held the policy was delivered; whether ztunnel re-checked it and let it pass, or never re-checked it, this record cannot tell (Interpretation). `istioctl ztunnel-config connections` was read at 04:24:06Z, after both proxies' connections to the worker had closed (04:24:01.963Z and 04:24:03.546Z), so it could not have listed either and says nothing about them. **The refused work items reached nothing:** the worker recorded 0 arrivals between 04:22:03.331Z and 04:36:17Z, the window of every refused send, and each refused `messageId` occurs 0 times in its whole log (`worker-arrivals.txt`). **After removal** (next entry's Method): all three paths delivered again.
- Interpretation: as documented for the recipe, and two readings it does not state. The policy admitted the path through `agw-central` and refused both paths that bypass it — "a policy on the destination workloads that allows only that identity denies any client that reaches them without first passing through the waypoint" — and on this topology the second bypass is the lab's own ingress: it dials the worker pod rather than the Service, so it arrives at the worker's ztunnel as itself, and the recipe closes the out-of-cluster path to the worker together with the direct one. ztunnel's refusal names the identity each caller arrived with, which is all this layer has, and in this lab that identity separates no caller: every lab workload runs as `ns/lab/sa/default`, so the load client through `agw-central` and the curl pod dialling direct carried one identity, and one was admitted and the other refused for the path each took; whatever `agw-central` delivers arrives as `agw-central`, so any workload that can address the worker Service passes. The policy separated paths, not callers. The first reading the documentation does not state is about a connection that was already open: one connection opened 18 s before a `WorkloadSelector`-scoped ALLOW policy was not closed when ztunnel received the policy, and the A2A request it carried 59 s later was delivered, while new connections under the same policy had been refused half a second before. That is the shape the STRICT record found for `PeerAuthentication` on 2026-09-12 (an XDS stream opened before the policy), and it means a policy's first readings on a live cluster can depend on what connections the proxies are holding. It is not what ztunnel 1.31.0 is built to do. Its `PolicyWatcher` (`src/proxy/connection_manager.rs` l.345-384 at tag `1.31.0`, from PR #772 "close connections which violate policy after updates", merged 2024-02-05, after issue #311 "Determine if RBAC updates should drain") re-runs the authorization check on every tracked inbound connection on every policy change, closes those now denied and logs "connection {} closed because it's no longer allowed after a policy update" at `info`; each HBONE connection is registered for it (`src/proxy/inbound.rs` l.272-280, "ensure rbac conditions are maintained for the duration of the connection"); and its unit test `test_policy_watcher_lifecycle` (l.615) drains a connection when a policy is inserted where none existed. Whether the watcher ran here and passed the connection or never ran, this record cannot tell: this run's ztunnel reads were filtered by address and were not searched for that line. A candidate cause — A HYPOTHESIS FROM READING THE SOURCE, NOT A READING: the re-check takes namespace- and mesh-scoped policies from ztunnel's current state but workload-scoped ones from the destination workload as it was stored when the connection opened (`src/state.rs` l.584-611, `let workload = wl.authorization_policies.iter()` with `wl = &ctx.dest_workload`; that `Arc<Workload>` is captured at CONNECT, `src/proxy/inbound.rs` l.434-437, and is left out of the connection's identity, `src/state.rs` l.154-160). C-3's policy has a selector, so istiod scoped it `WorkloadSelector` (`pilot/pkg/serviceregistry/ambient/authorization.go` l.425-432 at `1.31.0`) and delivered its name to the worker in the 276 B workload update beside the 91 B policy update; a workload stored before that update names no policy, so the re-check would pass. The upstream test's policy is `Scope::Global` (l.671), which is read from state and would not show this. Not covered by C-3: the orchestrator, the Python receiver, which the policy did not select; one work item per path, the ingress's two apart; and one pre-policy connection. The second reading the documentation does not state is what a refused caller is told, which differs by path and never names a policy: a transport reset with no HTTP status when dialling direct, a 503 carrying "Connection reset by peer" from the ingress, and — in C-4 — a 503 carrying "401 Unauthorized" on the tunnel from `agw-central`; only ztunnel's own line says a policy refused it, and that line names none.
- Follow-up: a CANDIDATE FOR A REPRODUCTION under rule 11, not a draft. Against ztunnel 1.31.0's own design this looks like a project gap: a connection opened before a selector-scoped ALLOW policy that excludes its caller was not closed. The isolating shape: in a namespace of its own, one connection opened before a selector-scoped ALLOW policy and one opened before a namespace-scoped ALLOW policy with no selector, each policy excluding its connection's caller, with ztunnel's log read for the watcher's "no longer allowed after a policy update" line; the source predicts that only the namespace-scoped policy closes its connection. `docs/upstream/` holds no draft: a draft needs the reproduction first, and the reproduction and any draft are the author's call.

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2

The two runs of the committed script added 4 Completed loadgen Job pods to the 12 found at the start. **After removal:** `g2c-c34after-worker` and `g2c-c34after-orchestrator` 1/1/1/1/1 `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`; driver direct and ingress 200/200, 1/1/1/1/1 each.
- Interpretation: as documented, and the cluster shows how the documented sentence comes about. The page says such a policy fails safe "by becoming a `DENY` policy"; what istiod handed ztunnel was not a DENY policy but the same ALLOW policy with its only rule omitted — `rules: []` — and an ALLOW policy that exists with no rule allows nothing, so the GET the rule named was refused as well as the POST, on every path, including the one C-3 admitted. Of the outcomes the method separated, the rule was neither refused nor enforced, and it did change something — it closed the worker to everyone — which is the documented fail-safe and the one outcome in which a narrower rule leaves the workload less reachable than C-3's policy without the operation rule. It was not silent: the status names the attribute it found and says "more restrictive than requested". But that message is the only place it is said. The condition reads `ZtunnelAccepted` `"True"`, istiod's log carries no warning, and no caller is told a policy refused it: `agw-central`'s access line says `401 Unauthorized` on the tunnel and ztunnel's lines name no policy. For C's question this is the ztunnel row's answer for the shape tested: this layer could not express "one operation refused, another allowed" even for two requests that differ by HTTP method, before the JSON-RPC body is reached at all, and the one-rule ALLOW policy that asked it to refused everything it selected. Other shapes are treated differently by istiod's own source (`pilot/pkg/serviceregistry/ambient/authorization.go` at `1.31.0`, l.455-476 and l.481-489, and `handleRule` l.599-601, "L7 policies never match for ALLOW"): within an ALLOW policy only the rules that carry HTTP attributes are omitted, so the rules of a multi-rule policy that carry none still admit, and a "DENY policy with HTTP attributes is enforced without the HTTP rules". Not covered by C-4: `paths`, `hosts`, the `request.*` conditions, a DENY policy, a multi-rule ALLOW policy and the orchestrator; one work item per path.
- Follow-up: none. The candidate the method named — an HTTP rule reduced with no status saying so — did not occur: the reduction is stated in the policy's status condition, so there is nothing to reproduce.

## Experiment C / ztunnel / open connections — does ztunnel close a connection opened before an ALLOW policy that denies its caller, and does the policy's scope decide it?

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2
- Environment: kind
- Method: the reproduction the C-3 entry's Follow-up named as a candidate under rule 11, approved by the author on 2026-09-21. Everything ran in a throwaway namespace `c3r`, ambient-enrolled by the one label `lab` carries (`deploy/step-2-ambient-agw/namespace-ambient.yaml`), created at 19:29:49Z and deleted 19:37:29Z–19:38:05Z (`objects/`, `objects-created.txt`, `objects-deleted.txt`): a server Deployment from the worker image exactly as the lab runs it (the `kind.local/worker-…` reference read from `deploy/worker`; it was sent only agent-card GETs, which it answers from its static card, its `MODEL_BASE_URL` names a port nothing listens on inside the pod, and with no OTLP endpoint it sets up no tracing), and a client pod from the pinned `curlimages/curl:8.22.0`, both running as `ns/c3r/sa/default` on the node `agent-mesh-lab-worker`, so one ztunnel carried both sides. Two policies, identical but for the selector, each an ALLOW with one rule admitting `cluster.local/ns/c3r/sa/c3r-admitted`, a service account no pod runs as: (a) `c3r-selector`, `selector: app: c3r-server` (C-3's shape); (b) `c3r-namespace`, no selector. One repetition, by the driver `rep.sh` kept in the run directory: open ONE connection — busybox `nc` in the client, fed through `kubectl exec -i` from a FIFO the driver holds open, so each request is written once, when the driver writes it, on that one TCP connection — and send one agent-card GET on it; read the connection's identity at three layers (the client's socket by `netstat`, ztunnel's tracked connections by `istioctl ztunnel-config connections`, the server's `remote` in its ingress ledger); apply the policy by `kubectl apply -f`, then wait on ztunnel's own state until `istioctl ztunnel-config policy` holds it and, for (a), until `istioctl ztunnel-config workloads` lists it on the server — a condition read, not a timer; read the policy's status, ztunnel's copy, the server's policy list, the tracked connections, ztunnel's log and the client's socket; send the same GET again on the same connection; open a new connection with one `curl --retry 0`; read the server's ledger, the tracked connections and ztunnel's log again; close the held connection (EOF on nc's input); delete the policy and wait on ztunnel's state until it no longer holds it; read back the `AuthorizationPolicy` count; read istiod's log from the apply. One control with no policy (`none-1`), then (a) and (b) three times each, interleaved a, b, a, b, a, b, 19:32:22Z–19:35:44Z, each with a fresh connection and a fresh apply. Counts by `counts.py` from the run directory alone into `counts.csv`. The ztunnel source the brief cites was read at tag `1.31.0` (tag object `e6fdcc5b`) at 19:25:24Z and again at 19:41:51Z, each file with its sha256 and every cited line (`sources.txt`). After the throwaway namespace was deleted, the committed `gate2-single-clean.sh` (`RUN_ID=c3rafter`, `after/`). Versions read from the cluster and the lock files into `versions.txt`; no pin was changed — `istioctl` on the host now reads client 1.31.1 against control and data plane 1.31.0, where the pin audits of 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-19 recorded 1.31.0, and it was used here only to read ztunnel's admin dumps. No retry logic: nc sends what it is given once and has none, every curl this task wrote is `--retry 0`, and nothing re-sends. This task started no keep-awake and changed no power setting, and keep-awake is not claimed absent — in the run window 19:28:22Z–19:39:07Z `host-sleep.txt` counts Sleep=0, Wake=0, DarkWake=0, Maintenance=0, Wake Requests=0 and 101 assertion lines, 8 of them naming `caffeinate`, which is the agent harness's own.
- Result: run outputs under `experiments/runs/2026-09-21-c3r-open-connections/` (`counts.csv`; one directory per repetition with its `events.txt`, `readings.txt`, `ztunnel.txt`, `istiod.txt` and nc's own bytes; `window.txt`). **The connection's identity**, each repetition: the client's own port (nc's socket, `10.244.1.42:44845` in selector-1), the server's record of it (`remote 10.244.1.42:39439` on request 1 there), and ztunnel's tracked inbound record on the server, `10.244.1.42:35880 -> 10.244.1.41:8080` — the client-side ztunnel's pooled HBONE connection to the server's 15008, the same in all seven repetitions while the client's port and the server's record changed each time; the watcher line, where it appeared, names exactly that key. **Control, no policy:** both GETs 200 on the held connection, arriving at the server on one `remote`; the new connection 200. **(a) selector-scoped, 3 of 3:** status `ZtunnelAccepted=True`, reason `Accepted`, "attached to ztunnel"; istiod one push per apply, WDS 238 B and WADS 67 B to each of the two ztunnels (the WDS push to the worker's ztunnel stamped 21–46 µs before its WADS push each time), and per removal WDS 219 B and WADS `removed:1` 0 B; ztunnel's copy `scope: WorkloadSelector`, `action: Allow`, one rule `principals: [Exact: cluster.local/ns/c3r/sa/c3r-admitted]`, and the server's policy list `[c3r/c3r-selector, istio-system/istio_converted_static_strict]` (before the apply the second alone); ztunnel logged `handling RBAC update c3r-selector` and then **no watcher line and no close line for the held connection**: it stayed in ztunnel's tracked connections, the client's socket read `ESTABLISHED`, and **the second GET on it was delivered** — 200 on the held connection, the server's second arrival on the same `remote`, 536, 458 and 458 ms after ztunnel's `handling RBAC update` (both stamps on the cluster's clock). **The new connection was refused**: curl exit 56 "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer", ztunnel inbound `connection closed due to policy rejection: allow policies exist, but none allowed` and outbound `http status: 401 Unauthorized`, 0 arrivals at the server. The held connection ended when the driver closed it, at `info` with no error on either side. **(b) namespace-scoped, 3 of 3:** status the same; istiod one push per apply, **WADS 68 B and no WDS push**, and per removal WADS `removed:1` 0 B; ztunnel's copy `scope: Namespace` with the same action and rule, and the server's policy list unchanged, `[istio-system/istio_converted_static_strict]`; **the watcher line** `connection 10.244.1.42:35880(spiffe://cluster.local/ns/c3r/sa/default)->10.244.1.41:8080 (Kubernetes//Pod/c3r/c3r-server-…) closed because it's no longer allowed after a policy update`, at `info`, 197, 176 and 202 µs after `handling RBAC update c3r-namespace`, beside an inbound access line `error="connection closed due to policy change"`; the server-side record left ztunnel's tracked connections, and the client's socket read `CLOSE_WAIT` — the peer's FIN received — before the second GET was written. **The second GET was not delivered**: busybox nc kept running after the FIN while its input stayed open, so the driver wrote the GET into the closed connection; its bytes reached the client-side ztunnel, which logged the held connection's outbound close `error="while closing connection: send: io error: broken pipe"` 395, 392 and 388 ms after `handling RBAC update`, and the server recorded 1 arrival on the held connection's `remote`, request 1's. **The new connection was refused** as in (a), 0 arrivals. **Across the window** (ztunnel and istiod logs from 19:29:40Z, read at 19:37:13Z, `window.txt`): 3 watcher lines on the worker's ztunnel, all three in (b); 0 `skipping unknown policy` lines; 0 lines at `warn` on the worker's ztunnel, 0 at `warn` or `error` in istiod. **Removal:** 0 `AuthorizationPolicy` read back after each of the six; after the namespace's deletion `namespaces "c3r" not found`, ztunnel on both nodes holding only `converted_peer_authentication_agentgateway-ingress-metrics` and `istio_converted_static_strict`, 0 `c3r` workloads in ztunnel, 2 `PeerAuthentication`s STRICT, 0 retry stanzas. **After:** `g2c-c3rafter-worker` and `g2c-c3rafter-orchestrator` 1/1/1/1/1 `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`.
- Interpretation: the outcome is the one the source predicted — only the namespace-scoped policy closed its connection, 3 of 3 each way — and it departs from what ztunnel's `PolicyWatcher` is built to do (PR #772, "close connections which violate policy after updates", for issue #311). ztunnel's own state held the selector-scoped policy and listed it on the server before the second request, and new connections were refused under it, yet the connection opened before it went on carrying requests until its client closed it; under the namespace-scoped policy — same server, same client, and a second request that met the closed stream at the client-side ztunnel 388–395 ms after ztunnel handled the policy, where in (a) it reached the server 458–536 ms after (both on the cluster's clock) — the watcher closed the connection within a fifth of a millisecond. The hypothesis from the source is supported, not confirmed by this outcome alone, which two other readings would also fit. (1) The watcher reads current state, but ztunnel applied the WADS update before the WDS update, so its one re-check saw the server's old policy list: istiod stamped the WDS push first each time, but the order ztunnel applied them in was not read — it logs `handling RBAC update` at `info` and not the workload update — and no second policy change was made after the WDS landed to separate the two. (2) The watcher did not run for a WorkloadSelector-scoped update: the source calls `policies.send()` after every WADS update whatever the scope (`src/xds.rs` l.529), and the watcher ran within 0.2 ms on this same proxy for the namespace scope, but a re-check that passes leaves no line, so its run for (a) is not observed. What weighs between them is the source as read: `assert_rbac` takes namespace and global policies from state and workload-selector ones from `ctx.dest_workload` (`src/state.rs` l.584-611), the `Arc<Workload>` captured when the connection was accepted (`src/proxy/inbound.rs` l.434-437); at #772's merge (`b95e5dd2`) it fetched the destination workload from state on every call, and PR #1218 (merged 2024-08-23, `4de5e896`) moved the re-check to the captured workload while each new connection still fetches it from state (`src/proxy.rs` l.195-197, l.240-248 at `1.31.0`), which is why new connections were refused here — a reading of the history; older versions were not run. The cited lines read the same on `master` at `db40ece` (2026-09-18; `sources.txt`, the readings added in the review round). The C-3 case fits the same shape: its ingress connection was opened 18 s before a WorkloadSelector-scoped ALLOW that reached the worker's ztunnel as a 276 B WDS and a 91 B WADS push, and a request on it was delivered 59 s later. For C's question this is a property of the layer: Istio's own "allow only the waypoint's identity" recipe is a selector-scoped policy, so on ztunnel 1.31.0 it closes no connection already open when it arrives, and such a connection — a proxy's pooled one included, as the ingress's was in C-3 — lasts until an endpoint closes it, and ztunnel logs nothing for it. Not covered: one node, with one ztunnel on both sides; HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only; one client identity; ALLOW only (a selector-scoped DENY takes the same path in the source; not run); a root-namespace (global) policy; a waypoint on the path; the lab's own agents.
- Follow-up: `docs/upstream/ztunnel-policy-watcher-selector-scoped-policy.md` — the draft issue text rule 11 asks for, addressed to istio/ztunnel, Status "draft, not filed", with the minimal reproduction, the source lines, the counts, and the tracker search of 2026-09-21T19:41Z in istio/ztunnel and istio/istio (every query in `tracker-search.txt`; no existing issue or pull request reports this; #311, #772 and #1218 are the related ones). It is filed by the author, never by the lab's agents; its link is added beside this entry as a dated note when it is filed.

- Interpretation: the C-3R result holds with a server anyone can pull, run as the draft words it: on ztunnel 1.31.0 a namespace-scoped ALLOW closed the connection opened before it, a selector-scoped one did not, 3 of 3 each way, and new connections were refused under both. Changing the server from the lab's Go `net/http` worker (idle timeout 120 s) to nginx 1.30.5 (`keepalive_timeout 65`), with the draft's names, principal and client in place of C-3R's, changed no outcome count (closed or not, delivered or not, refused or not, arrivals): under B nginx answered the second request on the held connection, under A the second request never reached nginx, so the closing, or its absence, is ztunnel's and not the server's. The draft's steps ran without a change beyond filling in its placeholders (the image, `$REQ_PATH`, `$SERVER_POD_IP`, `<node>`, `<policy name>`); the numbers that differ from the draft's table are the push sizes, which follow the object names, and B's two-resource WDS push with the policy also listed on the client, recorded above and not explained. The timings are of the same order as C-3R's and not all inside its ranges: A's watcher line 148–182 µs against C-3R's 176–202 µs, A's outbound `broken pipe` 431–435 ms against 388–395 ms (no overlap), B's second request at the server 486–499 ms against 458–536 ms. The two in milliseconds include the driver's own reads between the apply and the send, so they bound when the connection was still usable, not how fast ztunnel acts. This run adds no source reading, and it does not separate the two other readings the C-3R entry names (the order in which ztunnel applied the WDS and WADS updates; whether the watcher ran for the selector-scoped update). Not covered, as in C-3R: one node, with one ztunnel on both sides; HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only; one client identity; ALLOW only; a root-namespace (global) policy; a waypoint on the path.
- Follow-up: none upstream. `docs/upstream/ztunnel-policy-watcher-selector-scoped-policy.md` is **not to be filed — the author's decision of 2026-09-21**: its Status line says so, it stays in the tree because the C-3R entry cites it, and one dated line in it records this run and the push difference. Nothing was opened, commented on or filed upstream. The client-list reading is recorded here only.

## Experiment B / both receivers / B-3, a clean stream — What do the three ledgers and the client count for one `SendStreamingMessage` with nothing disrupted?

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2 (the cluster of the first B-3 entry, read back once, `versions-readback.txt`)
- Environment: kind
- Method: on the cluster the entry above rebuilt, after its standard proof and its model-call row. Each repetition sent ONE `SendStreamingMessage` from the load client's new stream mode (MODE=stream; one request, no retry, resend or reconnect; `http.Client.Timeout` 0 with the 2-minute context as the bound, every other transport setting `internal/httpclient`'s). The load client dials what the card advertises (Go: `agw-central`, `lab/worker`; Python: the ingress, `lab/orchestrator-ingress`), the Job is the template of the entry above with MODE=stream, nothing is armed on the mock or the receivers, and the orchestrator runs in model mode as above. `make ledgers` ran as soon as the Job ended, and both proxies' access-log lines were collected beside it. 20 repetitions per receiver, one at a time (`rows.sh stream`). `counts.py` parses stamps, joins the ingress response line to its arrival on (method, JSON-RPC id, `ts_arrival`) and the execution `received` line to the arrival on its `messageId`, and reads the final state from the executor's `state` lines, not from the result line (whose `state` on a streamed dispatch is the first Task's).
- Result: `stream/summary.csv`, per receiver, 20 of 20, both receivers alike: **1 arrival (`SendStreamingMessage`), 1 received (joined on `messageId`), 1 execute, 1 task, 1 invocation (`ok`)**; the ingress response line `stream_end: complete`; the execution result line `stream_end: complete`; the executor's last state line `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`; the execution result line's own `state` `TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED`, the first Task's, as B-1 recorded it would be. `A2A-Version: 1.0` on every arrival and the card read `streaming: true` every time, so the SDK sent the streaming method and not the `SendMessage` it falls back to for a card without it. The client, 20 of 20 on each receiver: 4 events in the same order on both receivers, `task/SUBMITTED > status-update/WORKING > artifact-update > status-update/COMPLETED`, a terminal event seen, the body ending cleanly (`stream_end: eof`), no error, the end line's `taskId` the one the executor created, the Job complete. The model route: 1 line at `agw-central` per repetition, 200.
- Interpretation: as documented, on both SDKs. This is the first cluster count of a streamed request: B-1's ledger changes read `complete` at both ledgers of both receivers when nothing is disrupted, and one stream is one dispatch, one Task and one model call. The two receivers put the same four events on the wire in the same order. Not covered: the Python receiver's 15 s keep-alive ping, which sse-starlette sends by default as the preparation read it and which these streams, ending in about 0.2 s, were too short to carry. The 45-second Python streams of the next entry ended as counted there, but no reading here took their bytes, so whether a ping was on the wire is not read. Also not covered: anything disrupted, which is B-4 and B-5.
- Follow-up: none.

## Experiment B / both receivers / B-3, `SubscribeToTask` during a running task — Does ONE `SubscribeToTask`, sent by a separate Job while the Task runs, attach without a second execution, and what is its first event?

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2 (the cluster of the first B-3 entry, read back once, `versions-readback.txt`)
- Environment: kind
- Method: on the same cluster. Each repetition: the mock armed with the delay of the first entry (45 000 ms) for the work item; Job 1, ONE `SendStreamingMessage` (MODE=stream); as soon as Job 1's own first client line named the Task (read from the Job's log), Job 2, a separate Job and a separate process, ONE `SubscribeToTask` for that task id (MODE=subscribe, TASK_ID from Job 1's line). Job 2 carries the same work item in its `X-Logical-Work-Item-Id` header, since the request has no Message. Both Jobs ran to their end, the mock was reset, and the ledgers were collected at once (`make ledgers`, whose second arm collects the subscription's anonymous execution lines by the task id the work item minted; Job 2's client lines collected by the driver). There is no loop and no reconnect: a Job that failed would have been recorded, not re-sent. 20 repetitions per receiver (`rows.sh subscribe-running`). The timing is read from the receiver's own ledgers, parsed and joined on identity: the executor's `TASK_STATE_WORKING` state line, the ingress arrival line of the `SubscribeToTask` (joined on its `taskId`), and the executor's `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` state line.
- Result: `subscribe-running/summary.csv`, per receiver, 20 of 20, both receivers alike: **+1 arrival (`SubscribeToTask`) beside the 1 `SendStreamingMessage`, 0 new executes (1 in all), 0 new tasks (1 in all), invocations still 1 (`ok`, 45 000.2–45 009.6 ms)**. The subscription's `received` line joins its arrival on the task id, and its task id is Job 1's in every repetition. Its first event, at the client: **a `task` at `TASK_STATE_WORKING` with Job 1's task id**. The execution ledger's first `delivered` line for the subscription reads the same. Then `artifact-update > status-update/COMPLETED`, a terminal event seen, `eof`, no error, `http 200`, `text/event-stream` (`; charset=utf-8` at the Python receiver), `posts` 1 (the round trips the SDK made through the load client's outermost transport; the wire count is the ingress ledgers'), the Job complete. Job 1 read what the clean stream reads: 4 events, `complete` at both ledgers. The subscription's ingress and execution lines read `stream_end: complete` too, and the executor's final state is `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`. **Timing:** the subscription arrived 16.3–18.7 s after the executor's working line and 26.3–28.7 s before its completed line (Go 16 415.7–18 738.4 ms and 26 264.8–28 592.3 ms; Python 16 261.0–18 354.5 ms and 26 655.0–28 748.0 ms), so the Task was running at every arrival, 40 of 40. Of the ~17 s, 15.7–18.1 s is the driver applying Job 2 with `ko apply`: that is the gap between reading Job 1's first event and Job 2 applied, per the stamps in each repetition's `steps.txt`. The rest is the Job's start: from Job 1 applied to its first event read took 0.6 s.
- Interpretation: as documented, and what the preparation read from both SDKs' source. A resubscription attaches to the live execution and starts nothing: no second execute, no second Task, no second model call. The first event is the Task as it stands, working, with the id asked for (specification v1.0.1 §3.1.6, "MUST return a `Task` object as the first event"). Neither SDK repeated or dropped an event around the snapshot in these 40: the subscriber saw working in the snapshot and then the artifact and completed, no second working. In process, a2a-go's store can still read submitted when the executor has already yielded working (the load client's own test records it). On the cluster, with the second Job ~17 s later, it read working every time. Not covered: a subscription sent within a second or so of the Task starting; more than one subscription at a time; a subscription after the original stream was cut (B-4 and B-5); the second Job's latency when it is not built by `ko apply` at the moment of use, which B-5 will want shorter or measured again.
- Follow-up: none.

## Experiment B / both receivers / D3, `SubscribeToTask` on a terminal task — What does each SDK answer ONE `SubscribeToTask` for a Task already in a terminal state, and does the answer vary?

- Versions: k8s=v1.37.0@sha256:a1ed56cfb0e7b93589bdf97c8cd566405a265939e3620fc4f5de89adff580ae5 istio=1.31.0 agentgateway=v1.5.0 gateway-api=v1.6.2, experimental a2a-spec=3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991 a2a-go=v2.5.0 a2a-python=1.1.4 openai-python=3.16.2 (the cluster of the first B-3 entry, read back once, `versions-readback.txt`); the specification text read from `3303592588e388e62e0f69f701af531d2f4e3991` (v1.0.1), fetched in this task (`sources.txt`)
- Environment: kind
- Method: the author's row D3 (proposal notes, 2026-09-20), on the same cluster. Each repetition: nothing armed; Job 1, ONE `SendStreamingMessage`, run to its end (the Task `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, the stream closed, the pod exited); then Job 2, a separate process, ONE `SubscribeToTask` for the task id Job 1's end line named, `A2A-Version: 1.0`, the work item in the header. The wire answer is read from Job 2's end line: `http_status`, `content_type`, and `wire_error_code` / `wire_error_message`, the first JSON-RPC error object in the bytes the SDK read. Those are recorded by the load client itself, because an answer the SDK's SSE reader skips would otherwise leave no trace at the client. The SDK's own error text is recorded beside them. Recorded per repetition, as B-1 found they decide which text a2a-python returns: the resubscriptions that repetition had already sent for the task (from the receiver's ingress ledger, `SubscribeToTask` arrivals for the task id before this one), and the elapsed time from the executor's terminal state line to the subscription's ingress arrival, both parsed and joined on the task id. 20 repetitions per receiver (`rows.sh subscribe-terminal`); the brief asked for at least 10. Before writing, each project's tracker was searched (`tracker-search.txt`).
- Result: `subscribe-terminal/summary.csv`, per receiver, 20 of 20. Job 1 read what the clean stream reads (1 arrival, 1 execute, 1 task, 1 invocation, `complete` at both ledgers, 4 events, `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`). Job 2's `SubscribeToTask`: +1 arrival joined to its `received` line on the task id, 0 executes, 0 tasks, 0 invocations added. Every subscription was the **first** for its task (0 prior resubscriptions, 40 of 40). It arrived **19.2–24.5 s** after the terminal state at the worker (mean 20.2 s) and **19.4–22.7 s** after it at the orchestrator (mean 20.4 s). **The Go receiver (a2a-go v2.5.0), 20 of 20:** HTTP 200, `text/event-stream`, carrying the JSON-RPC error **`-32001` "task not found: no active execution"** (`TaskNotFoundError`). That it came as the stream's one event is by source (`a2asrv/jsonrpc.go` l.235–238 writes one error event and returns). The client keeps the first error it finds, and no subscription `delivered` line exists, 20 of 20. The SDK client reported the same text as an error, no event, and `stream_end: error`. The ingress response line reads `stream_end: complete`, and the execution result line `stream_end: error` with the same text. **The Python receiver (a2a-sdk 1.1.4), 20 of 20:** HTTP 200, **`application/json`, not an event stream**, carrying the JSON-RPC error **`-32602` "Task <task id> is in terminal state: 3"** (`InvalidParamsError`; `3` is the state's enum number). The a2a-go client read **no event and no error**: its iteration ended quietly, with `stream_end: eof`. The answer exists at the client only in the bytes its wire observer kept. The ingress response line carries no `stream_end`, because the answer was not a stream. The execution result line reads `stream_end: error` with the same text. The texts did not vary, apart from the task id, on either receiver. a2a-python's other text, `Task <id> is already completed.`, which B-1 measured locally for a subscription made while the finished ActiveTask was still registered, did not appear.
- Interpretation: both SDKs depart from the specification here, and each departs differently. The specification v1.0.1 lists `UnsupportedOperationError` (`-32004`) for a `SubscribeToTask` "attempted on a task that is in a terminal state" (§3.1.6 l.305, §9.4.6 l.2408, mapped at l.1185). a2a-go answers `TaskNotFoundError` for a task its store still holds: it looks for a live execution and finds none (`local_manager.go` l.134–140), and its handler wraps that in `ErrTaskNotFound` (`handler.go` l.371–374). a2a-python answers `InvalidParamsError`, from a new ActiveTask whose `start()` finds the stored Task terminal (`active_task.py` l.466–474). This is what the preparation read from source and what B-1 measured in unit tests; it is now counted on the cluster, through both proxies. The a2a-python text depends, by source and by B-1's local measurement, on whether the finished ActiveTask is still registered, not on how many resubscriptions came first. Under this row's timing (a new process about 20 s after completion, the original stream long closed) it was "is in terminal state" 20 times of 20. What would bring "is already completed" onto the cluster — a subscription arriving while the original stream's tap is still open — was not produced here. There is also a second difference, between the two SDKs rather than with the specification, which B-5's brief is to carry: a2a-python sends a refused subscription as a plain JSON answer, because it fetches the first event before it starts the stream, and a2a-go's client, which reads the body only as SSE, sees nothing at all. A client built on a2a-go that does not read the wire itself counts that refusal as an empty, clean stream. The specification text read here says how a streaming method's successful answer is framed, and not how its error is. Not covered: a Task that ended `FAILED`, `CANCELED` or `REJECTED` (only `COMPLETED` was reached); a second resubscription within a repetition; a subscription within the first second after completion; the `SendMessage`-to-a-terminal-task half of the same specification rule, which both trackers already carry.
- Follow-up: docs/upstream/a2a-go-subscribe-to-terminal-task-not-found.md (a draft comment for a2aproject/a2a-go#438, which already reports the a2a-go half); docs/upstream/a2a-python-subscribe-to-terminal-task-invalid-params.md (a draft comment for a2aproject/a2a-python#1205, whose `SubscribeToTask` case is named in a comment and not in the open fix #1207). Both are for the author to post. The a2a-go client's silent reading of a JSON answer to a streaming method found no issue in its tracker; it is not drafted here (reading-notes.txt).
